title: Name-Writing Station
strapline: The most important word a child ever writes is their own name.
intent: Children recognise and write their own name — the personal, motivating gateway into reading and writing.
Children learn that letters have names and sounds, starting with the special letters of their own name.
Children develop the fine control and left-to-right formation that name-writing rehearses.
Children build identity and belonging — 'this is mine, this is me' — through their written name.
Children begin to notice their friends' names and the letters they share.
implementation: Give every child a name card with a clear starting dot and, if helpful, a photo, kept at the station.
Offer many ways in — name in sand, in dough, on a chalkboard, over-writing, tracing, then free writing.
Start with the capital first letter and celebrate it: 'that's your special T, Toby-letter!'.
Let children register themselves by finding and placing their name each morning — a daily, purposeful write.
Model the letter formation without pressure, saying the letter names as you go.
Point out shared letters between friends — 'you both start with an S!' — building letter recognition.
Keep the bar low and the praise high; a first letter and a wobble of others is a real success.
key_questions: Can you find your name — which letter does it start with?
What is the first letter of your name called?
Whose name starts with the same letter as yours?
Can you write your special first letter?
Where does your name begin — this side or that side?

impact.text: Children recognise their own name and pick it out from others.
Children write their name or make a good attempt at it.
Children name and sound the first letter of their name.
Children form letters left to right with growing control.
Children notice shared letters in their friends' names.
Children take pride in their written name and want to write it.

enhancements: A self-registration board where children place their name on arrival.
Name cards in a rainbow of media — magnetic letters, dough mats, sand trays.
A photo-and-name matching game for the group.
Name pebbles or beads to build their name letter by letter.
A 'letters in my name' hunt around the room.
Chunky pencils, chalks and grippy pens for varied grips.

playing_exploring: Children explore their name in every material at the station.
They play with the shapes and sounds of their own letters.
active_learning: Children keep practising because the name is theirs and matters.
Registering themselves each day gives the writing a real job.
creating_thinking: Children connect letters, sounds and names, spotting shared letters.
They choose how to make their name and check it looks right.
